3. Small protrusions emerge in sequence at its lower-left, lower-right, and top.
4. The combined shape rotates once and becomes a triangle.
5. Two thick lines emerge successively from the triangle's left, enclosing it in a rectangle.
6. A wave fills the rectangle from bottom to top.
7. The filled rectangle expands to full screen, and Welcome appears.

0b4d4c2e26ca05a6:
Next came implementation, based mainly on 喵神's article and demo, “A Refactoring We Never Expected to See — An Analysis of the iOS 10 UserNotifications Framework,” plus WWDC 708 Advanced Notifications and its PDF.
In the service, we download the image supplied in the back-end push payload to a local folder and use it as an attachment.
Previously, our notifications displayed only a single alert. The JSON alert field can be a string or dictionary; a string corresponds to the dictionary's body. After iOS8.2, the dictionary can include title, subtitle, and other fields. We wanted to turn the old body into a title and put an article summary in the body. But changing aps.alert directly would make pre-8.2 devices display the summary. We found another solution: Notification Service can modify the content. Leave aps.alert unchanged and add separate title and body fields to the JSON. When the service receives the notification, read them and assign them to bestAttemptContent.title and bestAttemptContent.body.
